prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To put a real number on this case we need: (1) the unit's actual square footage, so the $275/sq ft figure can be converted into a total dollar value; (2) the actual price and terms of the 2015 Mostafavi offer that triggered the ROFR, since that (not current market value alone) sets the price Shaw was entitled to match; (3) either a current appraisal or the property's value at the time of breach, depending on which measure of damages Iowa applies to a ROFR breach, so the 'unrealized appreciation' gap can actually be calculated; and (4) any evidence of what A&M or Mostafavi would argue as an offset (e.g., carrying costs, taxes, or financing costs Shaw would have incurred had he purchased in 2015).
prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability for breach of the ROFR is essentially conceded, so the tenant should win on the breach itself absent a waiver finding, and the waiver/estoppel defense is closer to a coin flip than a strong bar given the different-party problem and Shaw's active pursuit of purchase rights against the successor owner. The failure-to-mitigate defense is unlikely to succeed. However, the damages theory as currently documented (an unanchored $275/sq ft figure with no square footage, no 2015 sale price, and no current appraisal) cannot support a reliable dollar recovery estimate without additional facts.

issues.label: Breach of Right of First Refusal

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court awarded the tenant $257,216 in damages plus post-judgment interest, using the tenant's damages methodology (unrealized appreciation, rent-versus-mortgage differential, lost principal) but valuing the unit at the $166.73 per square foot the third-party buyers paid rather than the $275 the tenant proposed. No attorney's fees. The Iowa Court of Appeals affirmed (2-1) on August 19, 2026, rejecting the estoppel-by-acquiescence and failure-to-mitigate defenses.
